text:
alex_support: customer says they tried to issue a refund via our chatflow, UI showed success but no refund in payments ledger :face_with_raised_eyebrow:
priya_infra: can you drop the original function payload and a link to the trace?
alex_support: pasted payload and trace root below
alex_support: ```json
{"user_id":"cus_1234","action":"refund","amount":5000,"currency":"USD","source":"chatflow_v2"}
```
sam_ops: quick glance at the trace — the function selector chose `payment_inspect` instead of `create_refund`. The selector confidence was 0.46 and both functions accept an `amount` field in their signatures. :eyes:
luis_eng: repro steps i used: POST /v1/functions/invoke with selector=auto + payload above -> response 200, body shows inspect result and no refund created. Attachment: small log snippet
luis_eng: ```
[INFO] selector: auto -> chosen_tool: payment_inspect (confidence=0.46)
[INFO] invoke: payment_inspect args={"transaction_id":null,"amount":5000}
[INFO] no refund recorded for user cus_1234
```
priya_infra: looks like a schema overlap: inspect has optional amount/note args to support ad-hoc checks for amounts, which collides with create_refund's amount param. Selector is currently fuzzy by default. :face_with_monocle:
alex_support: customer hit this in prod on 2024-11-19 22:11 UTC; logged billing incident INC-9821
priya_infra: short-term mitigation: set routing preference to prefer exact alias matches for 'refund' and lower fuzzy threshold to 0.3 for payments namespace. I can push a small config toggle to staging now.
deploy-bot: staged config change applied: prefer_exact_alias=true, payments.fuzzy_threshold=0.30 (deploy id d-20241120-09)
nora_support: i'll let the customer know we toggled routing and will retry their refund, thanks
luis_eng: opened ticket INF-4123 with stack traces, function signatures, and suggested signature tightening (remove optional amount from payment_inspect). CC @backend-team
alex_support: quick repro curl for support/devs to reproduce locally:
alex_support: ```bash
curl -X POST 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/functions/invoke' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"tool_selector":"auto","payload":{"user_id":"cus_1234","action":"refund","amount":5000}}'
```
priya_infra: watching routing metrics for next 30m and will rollback if we see regressions. Long term we should: 1) make diagnostic logs include selector features, 2) enforce non-overlapping stable aliases, 3) require explicit alias in high-risk ops like refunds.
alex_support: customer retried after staged change and reported refund posted successfully. marking incident mitigated, leaving INF-4123 for the follow-up work. :white_check_mark:
